pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The balance sheet changed character in 2026. Principal debt rose from USD 600.0 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,235.0 million at 2026-09-30 to fund USD 5,323.6 million for Amicus, using USD 850.0 million of 5.5% senior unsecured notes, USD 2,800.0 million of senior secured term loans and cash on hand, with no equity issued [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Cash and investments fell from USD 2,052.9 million to USD 736.0 million [CP-1 liquidity; Documentary Fact]. The 65.8% of debt that is variable-rate is secured and amortizing, and the remaining 34.2% is fixed-rate (derived, Analyst Interpretation).

2. Earnings on the new perimeter are not yet visible in trailing figures. Filed LTM EBITDA of USD 378.8 million (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) implies total debt to EBITDA of 11.18x and net debt to EBITDA of 9.24x; adding back impairment, the ROCTAVIAN inventory write-off and acquired IPR&D, an analyst construct, gives USD 923.0 million, 4.59x and 3.79x [CP-1 chart data; Analyst Interpretation]. Amicus contributed revenue of USD 336.4 million and a net loss of USD 239.4 million from 2026-04-27 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. No pro forma EBITDA is supplied, so combined run-rate leverage is Not calculable.

3. Management defines its target differently and points to a lower level. In August 2026 management targeted gross leverage below 2.5x by mid-year 2027, defined as undiscounted debt over projected four-quarter adjusted EBITDA before depreciation, amortization and stock-based compensation [CP-1A; Management Language]. A backward-looking approximation of that definition gives USD 598.4 million of LTM EBITDA and 7.08x gross leverage [CP-1A calculation; Analyst Interpretation]. Reaching the target would need projected EBITDA of about USD 1,436 million if the May 2027 notes are paid in cash and scheduled amortization is made, or USD 1,694 million at current principal, which is 2.40x to 2.83x the LTM approximation [CP-1A; illustrative arithmetic]. Whether projections support this is Not calculable.

4. Liquidity covers the near term but rests on the revolver. Cash of USD 736.0 million plus an undrawn USD 600.0 million revolver is USD 1,336.0 million, which is 2.02x the USD 660.0 million of debt due in the next twelve months on the derived schedule (USD 15.0 million of term loan amortization in Q4 2026, USD 45.0 million in the first three quarters of 2027 and the USD 600.0 million convertible); cash alone is 1.12x [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Trailing operating cash flow less capex of USD 557.9 million adds funding capacity, but cash interest paid of USD 69.7 million understates the run-rate [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The revolver is available only subject to compliance with the credit agreement [CP-1; Documentary Fact].

5. The interest burden is the sharpest pressure point. Q3 2026 coupon interest was USD 52.7 million, or USD 210.7 million annualised, compared with USD 598.4 million of LTM EBITDA on the company's adjusted definition (2.84x), USD 378.8 million on filed EBITDA (1.80x) and USD 923.0 million on the analyst-adjusted basis (4.38x) [CP-1; CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. A rise of 100 basis points adds about USD 27.9 million to annual interest expense on USD 2,785.0 million of variable-rate debt [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The covenant minimum of 3.00x interest coverage uses a definition that is not supplied, so these ratios are not the covenant test.

6. Covenant compliance is stated but not measurable. The Term Loan A and the revolver carry a 3.50x maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio, temporarily 4.00x for certain acquisitions, and a 3.00x minimum Interest Coverage Ratio, with compliance stated at 2026-09-30 [CP-1 covenants; Documentary Fact]. Reported ratios and definitions are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. The analyst-adjusted net leverage of 3.79x sits close to the leverage maximum but the covenant definition probably uses pro forma and other adjustments, an inference that cannot be tested.

7. Capital is still flowing to acquired research. Acquired IPR&D was USD 287.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 221.0 million in Q3 2025; the Alesta acquisition (USD 303.4 million) and the BMN 450 license (USD 70.0 million upfront, up to USD 405.0 million in milestones) followed the leverage target, full-year guidance was cut on the two charges, and cash fell by USD 138.0 million in Q3 [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. This is a pattern of three pipeline-led deals, Inozyme, Alesta and BMN 450, in about fifteen months beside the Amicus deal, which constrains deleveraging speed [Analyst Interpretation].

8. Claims outside debt are material but known. Firm purchase commitments are USD 768.8 million (USD 291.1 million in 2026); contingent milestones judged reasonably possible are USD 485.5 million, plus Dimerix up to USD 510.0 million and Alesta up to USD 215 million, listed separately and not summed; FY2025 lease liabilities were USD 45.7 million; restructuring accruals are USD 47.7 million [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. There is no pension, factoring or supply-chain finance disclosure.

runs.text: Strengths. First, the franchise is profitable and cash-generative at the gross level: derived gross margin was 80.0% in Q3 2026, 78.3% in the nine months and 77.7% in FY2025, and trailing operating cash flow less capex was USD 557.9 million, which funds interest and amortization before new acquisitions [CP-1, CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. Second, revenue is spread over nine marketed products and several regions: the largest product, VOXZOGO, is 23.9% of Q3 2026 revenue, the United States is 36.8% and Europe 38.1% of company-marketed net product revenue, and Q3 2026 revenue grew 32% year on year, mainly from the acquired products [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Third, near-term liquidity is adequate: USD 1,336.0 million against USD 660.0 million of debt due within twelve months, and no maturity above USD 60.0 million a year between 2028 and 2030, which is amortization only [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Fourth, the company has never paid a dividend, has no documented repurchases and funded Amicus with debt and cash instead of distributions, so no cash has been extracted by shareholders [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Fifth, most debt is long dated: USD 2,785.0 million of term loans mature in 2031 and 2033 and USD 850.0 million of notes in 2034 [CP-1; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. First, leverage is high and its true level is unproven; trailing EBITDA includes five months of Amicus and every adjusted measure here is analyst-derived or management language, and the covenant definitions are unknown, so headroom cannot be shown [CP-1, CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. Second, earnings are volatile because of acquired IPR&D, which was USD 287.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 221.0 million in Q3 2025, and Q3 2026 produced an operating loss of USD 82.1 million and a net loss of USD 122.8 million [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Third, the interest burden is large against earnings, with annualised coupon interest of USD 210.7 million and USD 2,785.0 million of floating-rate debt [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Fourth, concentration: the top three customers are 34% of Q3 2026 net product revenue, VOXZOGO and VIMIZIM together are 45.0% of total revenue, GALAFOLD and POMBILITI are made by single-source third parties, and large government orders shift between quarters, which management cited for the November 2026 revenue guidance cut [CP-1A; Management Language]. Fifth, the asset base is intangible-heavy: goodwill of USD 666.4 million and intangible assets of USD 4,777.2 million are 47.1% of total assets of USD 11,569.2 million, and equity less goodwill and intangibles is USD 812.4 million, so balance-sheet protection for creditors relies on the cash flows of the acquired products rather than tangible assets (derived, Analyst Interpretation). Sixth, the structure ranks the secured term loans first on substantially all assets, with unnamed subsidiary guarantors; the position of the unsecured 2034 Notes and the subordinated 2027 Notes against guarantor assets cannot be determined, a mechanic that bears on recovery prospects without implying an outcome [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Seventh, the information base lacks executed legal documents, reported covenant ratios, projected EBITDA and ratings [CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A; Insufficient Information].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transaction is the acquisition of Amicus Therapeutics, Inc., a publicly traded biotechnology company, completed on 2026-04-27 under a merger agreement dated 2025-12-19. Amicus became a wholly owned subsidiary and brought GALAFOLD, POMBILITI + OPFOLDA and the BMN 820 candidate for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, with U.S. rights held under an assumed Dimerix license of up to 510.0 million in milestones (Q3 10-Q page:14, page:32; exhibit list Q3 10-Q page:123). Total consideration was 5,323,561 thousand: 4,563,463 paid to shareholders, 142,636 for restricted and performance stock units, 62,946 for the pre-combination part of stock options, 121,596 of seller transaction costs and 432,920 to repay Amicus debt including a prepayment penalty and accrued interest (page:14-15). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and includes intangible assets of 4,750,000, goodwill of 469,786 and a deferred tax liability of 577,589 (page:15-16). The intangibles are GALAFOLD at 3,000,000 over 11 years, POMBILITI + OPFOLDA at 1,450,000 over 12 years and the BMN 820 research asset at 300,000, which is not amortized (page:16). Acquisition-related costs of 32.8 million were expensed in selling, general and administrative expense in the nine months (page:14).

The financing was cash on hand and non-convertible debt, with no equity issued (page:14). First, in December 2025 the company signed a commitment letter for a 364-day senior secured bridge of up to approximately 3.7 billion; it was reduced to 2.8 billion when the 2034 Notes were issued and to zero when the term loans were signed (page:25). Second, in February 2026 (indenture dated 2026-02-12) the company issued 850,000 thousand of 5.5% senior unsecured notes due 2034-02-15, with interest payable on February 15 and August 15 from 2026-08-15, net proceeds of 832.3 million after 17.7 million of issuance costs, held in escrow until the Amicus close (Q3 10-Q page:25; Q1 10-Q page:13, page:17). The notes were not registered under the Securities Act (page:25), and a change of control repurchase feature exists for them (page:103). Third, on 2026-04-27 the company entered a senior secured credit agreement with Citibank, N.A. as administrative and collateral agent: an 800.0 million Term Loan A due 2031-04-27, a 2.0 billion Term Loan B due 2033-04-27 and a 600.0 million revolver due 2031-04-27, with issuance costs of 46.2 million (Q3 10-Q page:23-25; Q2 10-Q page:118). Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors (Q3 10-Q page:50). The guarantors are not named. The 2024 unsecured 600.0 million revolver was terminated (Q2 10-Q page:43). The 1.25% convertible notes of 600,000 thousand due May 2027 stay outstanding. The company says it used the notes proceeds, the term loans and approximately 1.7 billion of cash on hand to pay the consideration (page:47). A bridge commitment fee of 22.8 million was expensed (page:23). The cash flow statement ties to this: proceeds from borrowings were 3,650,000, the equal of 850,000 plus 2,800,000, and cash paid for the business combination net of cash acquired was 5,067,630, equal to total consideration less the 255,931 of Amicus cash acquired (page:10, page:15).

Liquidity effect: cash and investments fell from 2,052,851 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 736,007 at 2026-09-30, and principal debt rose from 600,000 to 4,235,000 (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:22, page:45). Management states a target of gross leverage below 2.5 times by mid-year 2027, a year earlier than the timeline given at announcement, supported by profitability growth, defined as undiscounted debt divided by projected four-quarter non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which is income from operations excluding depreciation, amortization and stock-based compensation (Q2 release page:3, page:10). That statement is Management Language, was made on 2026-08-06 and is not repeated in the November release. Management also states approximately 280 million of GAAP cost synergies, about 220 million on a non-GAAP basis, fully realized in 2028 (Q3 release page:3). The company announced restructuring tied to Amicus: severance of 29,478 in Q3 2026 and 82,618 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:30). Since the Amicus close the company has also completed the Alesta acquisition on 2026-08-31 for 303.4 million with 282.3 million expensed as acquired research and up to 215 million of milestones, and agreed in October 2026 the BMN 450 license with a 70.0 million upfront payment and up to 405.0 million of milestones (Q3 10-Q page:18, page:34). The scheduled maturity of the 2027 Notes, 600.0 million, is the first refinancing event; the notes are convertible at 137.47 per share and otherwise payable in cash (10-K page:206; Q3 10-Q page:48). No transaction source other than the filings is supplied: the merger agreement, credit agreement, indentures and supplemental indenture are exhibits incorporated by reference and their text is not in the pack, so legal terms, baskets and guarantor lists are Not supplied.

fields.value: The financial base is usable for the credit snapshot but it is a two-perimeter base, and every ratio must be read with that in mind. FY2025 is the audited pre-Amicus company with 600,000 thousand of convertible notes, net cash after investments and a derived EBITDA of 489,035 thousand. From 2026-04-27 the company consolidates Amicus, funded by 850,000 thousand of 5.5% notes, 2,800,000 thousand of secured term loans (since reduced to 2,785,000 thousand by one quarterly repayment on each loan) and cash on hand, so principal debt at 2026-09-30 is 4,235,000 thousand. Earnings on the new perimeter are only partly in the trailing twelve months. On the filed numbers, derived EBITDA for LTM Q3 2026 is 378,821 thousand, which gives total debt to EBITDA of 11.18x and net debt to EBITDA of 9.24x. Two items depress that EBITDA and are not recurring in the same way: the LTM includes impairment of assets and a ROCTAVIAN inventory write-off of 119,208 booked in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-K page:155), and it includes acquired IPR&D expense of 287,685 thousand in Q3 2026. Adding those back, as an analyst-derived measure and not a company figure, gives 922,962 thousand, total debt to EBITDA of 4.59x and net debt to EBITDA of 3.79x. Neither figure is pro forma for a full year of Amicus, and the covenant definition, which is not printed, may differ from both. Cash interest cover is 5.43x on the filed LTM basis but cash interest of 69,721 thousand is not a run-rate: annualised Q3 coupon interest is 210,732 thousand. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is cash of 736.0 million plus 600.0 million undrawn on the senior secured revolver, a total of 1,336.0 million. The 2027 Notes of 600,000 thousand are the next large maturity and are due in May 2027. The company states that the compliance tests on Term Loan A and the revolver were met. The view is therefore a clear debt and liquidity picture with an unresolved earnings run-rate, and the earnings gap is the main limit on every leverage conclusion.

fields.value: EBITDA is not reported by the company. This handoff defines it as income from operations plus the depreciation and amortization line of the cash flow statement. That D&A line is larger than the intangible amortization shown in operating expenses (177,433 in 9M 2026) and appears to include it, but the filing does not itemize the line. Inventory step-up amortization is recognized in cost of sales (29.2 million in 9M 2026, page:17) and is not separately identified in the D&A line, so EBITDA here is probably after step-up. The company's non-GAAP income adds back amortization, stock-based compensation, step-up and acquisition and restructuring costs, but does not add back acquired IPR&D (Q3 release page:12), so management itself treats the IPR&D charge as an operating cost. The adjusted EBITDA used above is therefore an analyst construct and a stricter test is the unadjusted one. Adjusted EBITDA also relies on the ROCTAVIAN inventory write-off appearing only in FY2025: no such line appears in the 2026 or 9M 2025 cash flow statements, so it is treated as nil there with that limitation; the 10-K places the write-off in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-K page:155).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin is a global rare-disease biotechnology company that discovers, manufactures and sells enzyme therapies and peptide medicines, reports one operating segment, and has no sponsor. Its credit story changed in 2026: it bought Amicus on 2026-04-27 for 5,323,561 thousand, adding GALAFOLD for Fabry disease and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA for Pompe disease, and financed it with debt and cash instead of equity, taking principal debt from 600,000 thousand to 4,235,000 thousand. Revenue is spread across nine marketed products, with VOXZOGO and VIMIZIM the largest in Q3 2026, but three customers account for about a third of net product revenue and ALDURAZYME depends on a Sanofi arrangement with change-of-control termination rights. Ownership is public with 28 holders of record at 2026-02-19, no controlling holder was found in the pack and no dividends have ever been paid, so there is no documented extraction. Documented capital allocation is mixed: since 2025 the company has made three pipeline-led deals, Inozyme, Alesta and the BMN 450 license, alongside the large Amicus transaction, while management states a target of gross leverage below 2.5 times by mid-year 2027 on its own projected adjusted EBITDA definition. That target is management language and the pack gives no projected adjusted EBITDA, so whether it is achievable cannot be tested here. Transaction-specific legal terms, guarantors and ownership percentages are not supplied. The view for the committee is a diversified but concentrated-customer rare-disease franchise that has moved to a levered, acquisition-driven profile with unproven deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction is the acquisition of Amicus Therapeutics, Inc., a publicly traded biotechnology company, completed on 2026-04-27 under a merger agreement dated 2025-12-19. Amicus became a wholly owned subsidiary and brought GALAFOLD, POMBILITI + OPFOLDA and the BMN 820 candidate for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, with U.S. rights held under an assumed Dimerix license of up to 510.0 million in milestones (Q3 10-Q page:14, page:32; exhibit list Q3 10-Q page:123). Total consideration was 5,323,561 thousand: 4,563,463 paid to shareholders, 142,636 for restricted and performance stock units, 62,946 for the pre-combination part of stock options, 121,596 of seller transaction costs and 432,920 to repay Amicus debt including a prepayment penalty and accrued interest (page:14-15). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and includes intangible assets of 4,750,000, goodwill of 469,786 and a deferred tax liability of 577,589 (page:15-16). The intangibles are GALAFOLD at 3,000,000 over 11 years, POMBILITI + OPFOLDA at 1,450,000 over 12 years and the BMN 820 research asset at 300,000, which is not amortized (page:16). Acquisition-related costs of 32.8 million were expensed in selling, general and administrative expense in the nine months (page:14).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financing was cash on hand and non-convertible debt, with no equity issued (page:14). First, in December 2025 the company signed a commitment letter for a 364-day senior secured bridge of up to approximately 3.7 billion; it was reduced to 2.8 billion when the 2034 Notes were issued and to zero when the term loans were signed (page:25). Second, in February 2026 (indenture dated 2026-02-12) the company issued 850,000 thousand of 5.5% senior unsecured notes due 2034-02-15, with interest payable on February 15 and August 15 from 2026-08-15, net proceeds of 832.3 million after 17.7 million of issuance costs, held in escrow until the Amicus close (Q3 10-Q page:25; Q1 10-Q page:13, page:17). The notes were not registered under the Securities Act (page:25), and a change of control repurchase feature exists for them (page:103). Third, on 2026-04-27 the company entered a senior secured credit agreement with Citibank, N.A. as administrative and collateral agent: an 800.0 million Term Loan A due 2031-04-27, a 2.0 billion Term Loan B due 2033-04-27 and a 600.0 million revolver due 2031-04-27, with issuance costs of 46.2 million (Q3 10-Q page:23-25; Q2 10-Q page:118). Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured by first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors (Q3 10-Q page:50). The guarantors are not named. The 2024 unsecured 600.0 million revolver was terminated (Q2 10-Q page:43). The 1.25% convertible notes of 600,000 thousand due May 2027 stay outstanding. The company says it used the notes proceeds, the term loans and approximately 1.7 billion of cash on hand to pay the consideration (page:47). A bridge commitment fee of 22.8 million was expensed (page:23). The cash flow statement ties to this: proceeds from borrowings were 3,650,000, the equal of 850,000 plus 2,800,000, and cash paid for the business combination net of cash acquired was 5,067,630, equal to total consideration less the 255,931 of Amicus cash acquired (page:10, page:15).

fields.value: Liquidity effect: cash and investments fell from 2,052,851 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 736,007 at 2026-09-30, and principal debt rose from 600,000 to 4,235,000 (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:22, page:45). Management states a target of gross leverage below 2.5 times by mid-year 2027, a year earlier than the timeline given at announcement, supported by profitability growth, defined as undiscounted debt divided by projected four-quarter non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which is income from operations excluding depreciation, amortization and stock-based compensation (Q2 release page:3, page:10). That statement is Management Language, was made on 2026-08-06 and is not repeated in the November release. Management also states approximately 280 million of GAAP cost synergies, about 220 million on a non-GAAP basis, fully realized in 2028 (Q3 release page:3). The company announced restructuring tied to Amicus: severance of 29,478 in Q3 2026 and 82,618 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:30). Since the Amicus close the company has also completed the Alesta acquisition on 2026-08-31 for 303.4 million with 282.3 million expensed as acquired research and up to 215 million of milestones, and agreed in October 2026 the BMN 450 license with a 70.0 million upfront payment and up to 405.0 million of milestones (Q3 10-Q page:18, page:34). The scheduled maturity of the 2027 Notes, 600.0 million, is the first refinancing event; the notes are convertible at 137.47 per share and otherwise payable in cash (10-K page:206; Q3 10-Q page:48). This module synthesizes the fundamental credit view from the accepted CP-1 financial base and CP-1A business and transaction pack, reopened against the pinned sources. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upstream handoffs are the evidence basis; the sources below were reopened to check the upstream figures that drive the view. The locator `page:N` is the extraction chunk, not the printed page.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin is a strong operating business that has become a leveraged acquirer, and its credit now depends on earnings catching up with debt. The strongest support is an 80.0% gross margin, nine marketed rare-disease products and USD 1,336.0 million of liquidity, with no large maturity before the May 2027 convertible. The weakest point is leverage: principal debt rose from USD 600 million to USD 4,235 million, and trailing EBITDA captures only five months of Amicus and large acquired-research charges. What decides the outcome is whether combined earnings reach roughly USD 1.4 billion to USD 1.7 billion, the level the management target implies, while cash keeps flowing to new acquisitions. Covenant headroom, guarantors and ratings are not supplied, so confidence is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The balance sheet changed character in 2026. Principal debt rose from USD 600.0 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,235.0 million at 2026-09-30 to fund USD 5,323.6 million for Amicus, using USD 850.0 million of 5.5% senior unsecured notes, USD 2,800.0 million of senior secured term loans and cash on hand, with no equity issued [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Cash and investments fell from USD 2,052.9 million to USD 736.0 million [CP-1 liquidity; Documentary Fact]. The 65.8% of debt that is variable-rate is secured and amortizing, and the remaining 34.2% is fixed-rate (derived, Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Earnings on the new perimeter are not yet visible in trailing figures. Filed LTM EBITDA of USD 378.8 million (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) implies total debt to EBITDA of 11.18x and net debt to EBITDA of 9.24x; adding back impairment, the ROCTAVIAN inventory write-off and acquired IPR&D, an analyst construct, gives USD 923.0 million, 4.59x and 3.79x [CP-1 chart data; Analyst Interpretation]. Amicus contributed revenue of USD 336.4 million and a net loss of USD 239.4 million from 2026-04-27 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. No pro forma EBITDA is supplied, so combined run-rate leverage is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Management defines its target differently and points to a lower level. In August 2026 management targeted gross leverage below 2.5x by mid-year 2027, defined as undiscounted debt over projected four-quarter adjusted EBITDA before depreciation, amortization and stock-based compensation [CP-1A; Management Language]. A backward-looking approximation of that definition gives USD 598.4 million of LTM EBITDA and 7.08x gross leverage [CP-1A calculation; Analyst Interpretation]. Reaching the target would need projected EBITDA of about USD 1,436 million if the May 2027 notes are paid in cash and scheduled amortization is made, or USD 1,694 million at current principal, which is 2.40x to 2.83x the LTM approximation [CP-1A; illustrative arithmetic]. Whether projections support this is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Liquidity covers the near term but rests on the revolver. Cash of USD 736.0 million plus an undrawn USD 600.0 million revolver is USD 1,336.0 million, which is 2.02x the USD 660.0 million of debt due in the next twelve months on the derived schedule (USD 15.0 million of term loan amortization in Q4 2026, USD 45.0 million in the first three quarters of 2027 and the USD 600.0 million convertible); cash alone is 1.12x [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Trailing operating cash flow less capex of USD 557.9 million adds funding capacity, but cash interest paid of USD 69.7 million understates the run-rate [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The revolver is available only subject to compliance with the credit agreement [CP-1; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. The interest burden is the sharpest pressure point. Q3 2026 coupon interest was USD 52.7 million, or USD 210.7 million annualised, compared with USD 598.4 million of LTM EBITDA on the company's adjusted definition (2.84x), USD 378.8 million on filed EBITDA (1.80x) and USD 923.0 million on the analyst-adjusted basis (4.38x) [CP-1; CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. A rise of 100 basis points adds about USD 27.9 million to annual interest expense on USD 2,785.0 million of variable-rate debt [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The covenant minimum of 3.00x interest coverage uses a definition that is not supplied, so these ratios are not the covenant test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Covenant compliance is stated but not measurable. The Term Loan A and the revolver carry a 3.50x maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio, temporarily 4.00x for certain acquisitions, and a 3.00x minimum Interest Coverage Ratio, with compliance stated at 2026-09-30 [CP-1 covenants; Documentary Fact]. Reported ratios and definitions are Not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. The analyst-adjusted net leverage of 3.79x sits close to the leverage maximum but the covenant definition probably uses pro forma and other adjustments, an inference that cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Capital is still flowing to acquired research. Acquired IPR&D was USD 287.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 221.0 million in Q3 2025; the Alesta acquisition (USD 303.4 million) and the BMN 450 license (USD 70.0 million upfront, up to USD 405.0 million in milestones) followed the leverage target, full-year guidance was cut on the two charges, and cash fell by USD 138.0 million in Q3 [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. This is a pattern of three pipeline-led deals, Inozyme, Alesta and BMN 450, in about fifteen months beside the Amicus deal, which constrains deleveraging speed [Analyst Interpretation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Claims outside debt are material but known. Firm purchase commitments are USD 768.8 million (USD 291.1 million in 2026); contingent milestones judged reasonably possible are USD 485.5 million, plus Dimerix up to USD 510.0 million and Alesta up to USD 215 million, listed separately and not summed; FY2025 lease liabilities were USD 45.7 million; restructuring accruals are USD 47.7 million [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. There is no pension, factoring or supply-chain finance disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, the franchise is profitable and cash-generative at the gross level: derived gross margin was 80.0% in Q3 2026, 78.3% in the nine months and 77.7% in FY2025, and trailing operating cash flow less capex was USD 557.9 million, which funds interest and amortization before new acquisitions [CP-1, CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. Second, revenue is spread over nine marketed products and several regions: the largest product, VOXZOGO, is 23.9% of Q3 2026 revenue, the United States is 36.8% and Europe 38.1% of company-marketed net product revenue, and Q3 2026 revenue grew 32% year on year, mainly from the acquired products [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Third, near-term liquidity is adequate: USD 1,336.0 million against USD 660.0 million of debt due within twelve months, and no maturity above USD 60.0 million a year between 2028 and 2030, which is amortization only [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Fourth, the company has never paid a dividend, has no documented repurchases and funded Amicus with debt and cash instead of distributions, so no cash has been extracted by shareholders [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Fifth, most debt is long dated: USD 2,785.0 million of term loans mature in 2031 and 2033 and USD 850.0 million of notes in 2034 [CP-1; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, leverage is high and its true level is unproven; trailing EBITDA includes five months of Amicus and every adjusted measure here is analyst-derived or management language, and the covenant definitions are unknown, so headroom cannot be shown [CP-1, CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. Second, earnings are volatile because of acquired IPR&D, which was USD 287.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 221.0 million in Q3 2025, and Q3 2026 produced an operating loss of USD 82.1 million and a net loss of USD 122.8 million [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Third, the interest burden is large against earnings, with annualised coupon interest of USD 210.7 million and USD 2,785.0 million of floating-rate debt [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Fourth, concentration: the top three customers are 34% of Q3 2026 net product revenue, VOXZOGO and VIMIZIM together are 45.0% of total revenue, GALAFOLD and POMBILITI are made by single-source third parties, and large government orders shift between quarters, which management cited for the November 2026 revenue guidance cut [CP-1A; Management Language]. Fifth, the asset base is intangible-heavy: goodwill of USD 666.4 million and intangible assets of USD 4,777.2 million are 47.1% of total assets of USD 11,569.2 million, and equity less goodwill and intangibles is USD 812.4 million, so balance-sheet protection for creditors relies on the cash flows of the acquired products rather than tangible assets (derived, Analyst Interpretation). Sixth, the structure ranks the secured term loans first on substantially all assets, with unnamed subsidiary guarantors; the position of the unsecured 2034 Notes and the subordinated 2027 Notes against guarantor assets cannot be determined, a mechanic that bears on recovery prospects without implying an outcome [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Seventh, the information base lacks executed legal documents, reported covenant ratios, projected EBITDA and ratings [CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A; Insufficient Information].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis: a high-margin, diversified rare-disease franchise with adequate near-term liquidity, whose creditworthiness over the next twelve to eighteen months depends on integrating Amicus, containing acquired-research spend and converting a debt-funded purchase into combined earnings that support a lower leverage level [Analyst Interpretation]. Assessment confidence: Medium. It is below High because the CP-1A gaps that carry weight for this module are open: no executed financing documents, no projected adjusted EBITDA, and management language on leverage that cannot be tested. CP-1A judged this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and logged no Critical gap.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is the operating cash generation: nine-month operating cash flow of 576,974 thousand after 244,514 of depreciation and amortization, an 80.0% gross margin, liquidity above the next twelve months of maturities, and Amicus products already contributing 200,416 thousand of Q3 revenue. If integration synergies of about 280 million (220 million non-GAAP) are realized and acquired research charges fall, EBITDA on the management definition could approach the level implied by the target. What would make that case win: a fourth quarter and first half of 2027 with adjusted EBITDA run-rate near 1.4 to 1.7 billion, the May 2027 notes repaid from cash, and a compliance certificate showing covenant headroom. What would make the cautious case win: further acquired research charges, order-timing misses like the November guidance cut, or a leverage ratio above 3.50x on the covenant definition.
